transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, I'm here because my sleep has basically just fallen apart lately. I'll lie in bed in my apartment for hours, you know, with my laptop closed, but I'm still mentally rechecking everything. Like work deadlines, my tuition payments, class assignments... it just doesn't stop. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really turned off. It's just exhausting.
When you finally do fall asleep, how long do you typically stay asleep before waking up?

I'm not exactly sure, honestly. Um, I try not to look at the clock when I wake up in the middle of the night, because seeing the time just makes me stress more about how soon I have to be up. So... I don't really know the exact number of hours. It just feels like it's never for very long before I'm awake again.
When you first get into bed at night, how long does it usually take you to fall asleep for the first time?

I'm not entirely sure about that either, to be honest. Um... it definitely feels like a really long time. I don't time it, but it feels like I'm just lying there for hours, tossing and turning and thinking about everything I need to get done. So I couldn't give you an exact number of minutes or anything, just... a really long time.

During the day when you're not trying to sleep, do you find yourself constantly worried or anxious about these things like work deadlines and tuition payments, or does the worry mainly happen at night when you're trying to fall asleep?

It's definitely during the day, too. Honestly, it's pretty much all the time. My mind just keeps jumping around from one thing to another. 

Like, I'll be worrying about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then it switches to whether I'm just wasting money on school, or... or whether my family will think I can't handle things. It's just constant. I basically treat every small issue that comes up like it could completely derail my whole future. So, yeah, it's definitely not just at night.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worry and difficulty sleeping? Has it been going on for a few weeks, or has this been happening for several months or longer?

It's been quite a while, definitely longer than a few months. I'd say it's been going on for about a year and three months now. That's right around the time I started taking an evening graduate certificate program, while still keeping my full-time analyst job. So, yeah, it's been happening ever since then.

During these times when you're worried, have you ever experienced sudden episodes where your heart starts racing, you feel like you can't breathe, or you have intense physical sensations of panic? Or is it more of a constant mental worry without those sudden intense physical episodes?

No, I don't really get those sudden physical episodes you're describing. My heart doesn't race like that, and I don't feel like I can't breathe. It's really just the constant mental worry, like you said. It's more of a steady, exhausting feeling of stress in my head rather than any intense physical panic attacks.
When you're having these worries during the day, do you feel like you're able to control them or stop them, or do they just keep happening no matter what you try to do?

I really can't stop them at all. I mean, I try. I try to tell myself to just stop and focus on one thing, like whatever I'm supposed to be doing at work. But it doesn't work. One worry just immediately leads to another. Before I know it, I'm checking my calendar, then my budget, and then going over my school assignments over and over again. I just get stuck in this loop instead of actually getting anything done.
Besides the mental worry and sleep problems, do you notice physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling restless or on edge, or excessive fatigue during the day?

Yeah, the fatigue is really bad. By midafternoon at the office, I just feel completely drained. It's like even doing simple things, like answering emails or just walking to the subway, takes so much effort. And it doesn't really get better... even when I try to rest on the weekend, it just doesn't seem to give me my energy back. I'm just tired all the time.
You mentioned fatigue, but I'm also curious about the opposite experience — do you find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or unable to sit still, even when you're trying to relax?

No, not really. I don't feel fidgety or like I can't physically sit still. It's actually kind of the opposite, since I'm usually just so drained. My body stays put just fine... it's really just my mind that's restless and won't stop going. So, no, I haven't noticed any pacing or feeling unable to sit down.

How much has this constant worry and difficulty sleeping affected your ability to do your job, keep up with school, or handle your daily responsibilities? Has it caused you significant problems in these areas?

It's causing a lot of problems, honestly. I’ve actually started missing work deadlines, which isn't like me at all. And I’m falling behind in my certificate classes, too. It's just... it's too hard to keep up with everything. 

And at home, I’ve pretty much stopped doing the routines that used to keep me grounded. Like, I used to do yoga, go running, and cook my own meals, but I just don't do any of that anymore. I've just stopped all of it.
Besides the fatigue and loss of interest in activities like yoga and running, have you noticed changes in your mood itself — like feeling persistently sad, empty, or hopeless about things?

No, I don't think so. I don't really feel sad or... empty. It's not like that. I mean, I'm just so overwhelmed and exhausted by my mind constantly racing, but I wouldn't say I feel hopeless about things. It's really just the constant worry, not sadness.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was elevated or unusually good — maybe lasting for several days or more?

No, I haven't ever felt like that. I don't get bursts of energy or feel unusually happy for days at a time. And I definitely don't feel like I need less sleep—I just can't get the sleep I need. So, no, nothing like that.
